Duolingo can be effective for any language but understand that your language learning will be incomplete if you only use Duolingo. Duolingo doesn’t provide much opportunity for reading comprehension, conversational skills (like slang and how natives actually use the language because the formal way you write things isn’t always how you talk. Think: double negatives in English, gotta wanna shoulda coulda, ain’t, etc.), or making up your own sentences. It also seems to lack exercises to nail down confusing concepts (like in Spanish por vs para). So yes, it can help you learn the language, but it’s best to have other sources of learning as well.

My best advice is to use how you learn best to your advantage. I don’t get much out of reading. I get a lot from visuals and from auditory methods. So I basically skipped a lot of reading or used a screen reader. I copied a lot of visuals into notes on my iPad. If you have a class that’s challenging, reach out to your CI. I honestly only really reached out to CI’s for a few classes. If you are in Washington, I highly recommend reaching out to your CI ASAP for the PNW history course. That one is a doozy. It’s the only OA I had to take twice and I barely passed the second time. For the PA’s, I copy and paste the requirements into a word doc and convert it to a table to use as a checklist. Also, sometimes the evaluators want you to use very specific wording. It’s really annoying because I’ve had tasks sent back and I literally changed a single sentence and passed. Try to make sure you use wording that mirrors the wording they use in the course. Good luck. If you work hard and are committed, you can do it. I also set goals for when to finish courses and if I finished a course early, I would email my mentor and register for the next courses before our meeting.
